Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.2: Kenyan indigenous games Board games (Optional)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Kenyan indigenous games Board games (Optional), part of Strand 12 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9 CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS.

Key inquiry question: when watching a virtual demonstration of board games. 1. How does indigenous board games enhance mental relaxation?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

A. identify types of indigenous board games played in Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan indigenous games Board games (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan indigenous games Board games (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Kenyan indigenous games Board games (Optional) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

• Responsibility: the learner takes on different roles during indigenous board games.

• Unity: the learner works with others in indigenous board games

(PCIs):

• Safety: the learner observes safety rules when playing indigenous board games.

• Health and Fitness: the learner improves fitness through indigenous board games for a healthy lifestyle.

Link to other learning areas:

• Mathematics: the learner keeps counting during indigenous board games.
